after: In this work, we integrated human microglial transcriptomics, model-derived glial programs, and network pharmacology to investigate YZDHD-related candidates in AD. By linking disease-associated genes with compound–target records, we identified candidate connections involving lactylation-associated metabolism, senescence-related transcription, and iron homeostasis. Increased senescence-associated and ferro-aging reference scores in amyloid-exposed microglia, alongside contrasting astrocytic iron responses, suggest that these programs may depend on cellular context. These associations provide a rationale for investigating whether YZDHD-related compounds could modulate interconnected glial responses in AD. However, limited human transcriptional convergence, nonsignificant primary network proximity, and variable virtual knockout responses warrant caution in assigning a mechanism to the preparation. Further studies should combine chemically characterized YZDHD with direct measurements of histone lactylation, senescence, iron handling and target engagement. Such studies could clarify whether the preparation affects these processes and, if so, in which direction. Our integrative analysis may help guide these experiments and refine multipathway pharmacological hypotheses for AD.

before:
In this study, we connected human AD microglial associations to model-derived glial programs and then examined YZDHD-related pharmacological candidates through source review, network analysis, structural assessment, and virtual knockout analysis. The human layer identified a directionally stable 244-gene subset under the prespecified analysis. Complementary models supported senescence-related, iron-handling, and lipid-peroxidation-associated responses, including five significant astrocyte modules. However, the integrated candidate analyses did not establish a validated pharmacological mechanism for the complete preparation. Their main contribution was to make the path from disease association to an experimentally testable hypothesis explicit.

The human and model layers answered different questions. The human cohorts identified expression features associated with AD across retained anatomical contexts, whereas iMGL and animal datasets characterized responses to defined experimental conditions. The failure of the predefined human module composites to meet the human meta-analysis FDR criterion therefore matters: it prevents model convergence from being presented as uniform activation of a human disease pathway. Even the 244-gene subset should be interpreted within its statistical construction. Its direction was preserved after cohort omission, but its significance was not required in every reduced analysis, and its meta-analysis did not explicitly model correlated regions within donors. Disease-associated astrocyte studies and experimental induction of reactive astrocytes by microglial factors likewise illustrate context-dependent glial responses; our cross-dataset similarities do not demonstrate the same communication mechanism (Habib et al. 2020; Liddelow et al. 2017).

Lactylation illustrates why mechanistic specificity must be maintained during integration. The H4K12la anchor and the H3K18la/SASP bridge concern distinct modifications and experimental systems (Pan et al. 2022; Wei et al. 2023). Their inclusion provides complementary biological context, but does not demonstrate a continuous H4K12la-driven senescence mechanism in human AD microglia. RNA-based proxies cannot identify occupancy at a histone residue. The absence of human confirmation leaves the relevance of this model mechanism unresolved; it does not demonstrate the absence of lactylation biology. The original demonstration of histone lactylation established a metabolite-linked chromatin modification in other cellular contexts, reinforcing the need for residue- and system-specific validation (Zhang et al. 2019).

Iron-related programs were similarly context dependent. iMGLs showed increased uptake and decreased export scores after amyloid exposure, while the astrocyte model showed the opposite directions. This contrast supports separate treatment of cellular states, species, sampling times, and assay layers. It also argues against collapsing iron uptake, storage, export, and ferritinophagy into a single undifferentiated score. Ferro-aging-like expression can be useful as an operational reference, but RNA scores do not establish ferroptosis, iron-driven causality, or direct lipid-peroxidation flux. The original primate framework (Liu et al. 2026a) remains an external biological reference rather than a mechanism automatically transferred to AD glia. Its subsequent correction concerned source data for Figure S2P; the correction notice states that the published figure, analyses, and conclusions remain unchanged (Liu et al. 2026b). The present analysis retained the selected Table S2 gene-set version. Direct ferroptosis studies link iron-dependent oxidative death and ACSL4-mediated lipid composition, while NCOA4 experiments distinguish ferritin cargo turnover from a general iron-response signature (Dixon et al. 2012; Doll et al. 2017; Mancias et al. 2014).

Pharmacological evidence also required distinctions beyond target overlap. Exact compound identity and source-reviewed experimental records narrowed the human intersection to five candidates, while the larger program-associated set contained twenty targets. Neither count identified a therapeutically beneficial action. CA2, for example, combined a negative disease expression association with inhibition records, creating a direction question that cannot be resolved by reversing the transcriptomic sign. LTA4H required attention to dual enzyme functions and ingredient provenance; PKM required isoform and site specificity. SNCA aggregation observations could not be equated with direct binding to a wild-type monomer. These qualifications define the experiments needed for each candidate.

The primary network result further constrained the formula hypothesis. The candidate target collections did not show significant proximity to the human association subset in the direct experimental-channel network. This result does not prove pharmacological inactivity, because coverage and source selection were incomplete. It does show that network proximity cannot currently serve as positive global support for the proposed human mechanism. Significant results for model programs were conditional annotations, particularly where members were shared between microglial and astrocytic modules. Structural calculations likewise provided local geometric assessments, with receptor-specific limitations involving metals, covalent sites, transporter conformations, and aggregation models.

The virtual knockout analysis showed that an interpretable computational response is not necessarily a stable or target-specific one. Several initial AD pathway observations diminished under donor omission, bootstrap resampling, or removal of translation-related annotation contributors. Reference comparisons revealed that high module disturbance could be shared by many perturbations within the same network. The matching correction improved expression support and numerical comparability, but the corrected responses remained insufficiently distinct to establish specificity. This distinction is useful for experimental design: it discourages selection based solely on one random network realization or a high unsigned perturbation percentile.

Cell identity remained another material limitation. Cell identity was assessed using source annotations and marker coexpression; comprehensive doublet and ambient-RNA correction was not performed. In particular, a weakly expressed target can be supported by relatively few cells even in a large background. Balanced sampling and a retained target list do not resolve uncertain cellular origin. Similarly, bootstrap replicates and two random seeds probe stability within the available data; they do not add independent biological donors. These issues are consistent with the broader need to preserve biological replication in single-cell inference (Squair et al. 2021). DoubletFinder, Scrublet, and SoupX exemplify methods designed to address doublet or ambient-RNA artifacts; they are cited as validation options and were not completed in this workflow (McGinnis et al. 2019; Wolock et al. 2019; Young and Behjati 2020).

Several additional constraints affect translation. The predefined ingredient list lacks verified dose, preparation, batch composition, and quantitative chemical measurements. Its database chemical space therefore cannot establish the constituents of the administered preparation. ADMET outputs are predictions, and blood–brain barrier estimates do not determine relevant unbound exposure. No formula exposure–potency comparison, direct target-engagement measurement, signed drug-induced state change, or rescue experiment was available. Spatial analysis did not identify a qualified dataset satisfying the prespecified inclusion criteria, preventing estimation of AD–control spatial effects or directed intercellular communication. This evidence gap cannot be interpreted as a null biological result. Experimental work on intracellular bioavailability shows why predicted physicochemical properties do not determine the drug fraction available to an intracellular target (Mateus et al. 2017).

The framework nevertheless supplies a practical basis for subsequent validation. A chemically characterized preparation could be tested at measured, relevant exposure levels in microglial and astrocytic systems. Candidate hypotheses should specify target identity and action direction before evaluation, with target engagement and perturbation/rescue measurements linked to prespecified endpoints. Lactylation, senescence, iron handling, and lipid-peroxidation-associated hypotheses require their respective direct measurements. For human inference, a covariance-aware synthesis of paired regional effects and stronger cell-identity verification would address remaining statistical and annotation limitations. Such experiments would determine whether the present associations can be converted into a pharmacologically coherent mechanism. Cellular thermal shift assays and live-cell kinase occupancy methods illustrate direct engagement measurements that could be selected after target- and assay-specific validation (Martinez Molina et al. 2013; Vasta et al. 2018).
after:
In this study, we integrated human microglial transcriptomics with model-derived glial programs and pharmacological records to investigate YZDHD-related candidates in AD. The directionally stable 244-gene subset provided a human disease reference, while five significant astrocyte modules and complementary microglial responses highlighted context-dependent biological programs. Together, these findings suggest that candidate evaluation may benefit from considering metabolic regulation, senescence-associated transcription and iron handling jointly. Their value lies in specifying biological questions and candidate connections that can be examined experimentally, with human associations and model mechanisms contributing different forms of evidence.

The relationship between human associations and model responses is central to interpreting these findings. Human postmortem expression reflects disease-associated states across anatomical contexts, whereas iMGL and animal datasets capture responses under defined experimental conditions. The absence of significant human module composites suggests that coordinated model responses may not generalize uniformly across human AD microglia. Differences in species, exposure duration, brain region and disease stage offer plausible explanations that would require targeted comparisons. The 244-gene subset may therefore be more useful as a reference for disease relevance than as a unified mechanistic pathway. Its direction persisted after cohort omission, although significance was not required in every reduced analysis and correlated regions within donors were not explicitly modeled. Disease-associated astrocytes and experimentally induced reactive astrocytes likewise illustrate how glial responses depend on their biological setting. Similarity between our datasets may motivate tests of intercellular communication, but does not identify its direction or mediators (Habib et al. 2020; Liddelow et al. 2017).

Lactylation offers a potential connection between metabolic state and chromatin regulation that could help explain persistent glial responses. The H4K12la and H3K18la/SASP findings provide complementary evidence from distinct modifications and experimental systems (Pan et al. 2022; Wei et al. 2023). In our analysis, this literature context supports investigating metabolic and inflammatory responses together, while leaving a continuous H4K12la-driven senescence mechanism in human microglia unresolved. Increased senescence-associated transcription after amyloid exposure could reflect overlapping inflammatory and stress responses, rather than durable cellular senescence alone. Distinguishing these possibilities would require direct chromatin measurements alongside functional senescence endpoints and temporal perturbation experiments. The broader discovery of histone lactylation supports this metabolic interpretation, although its consequences may vary with the modified residue and cellular context (Zhang et al. 2019).

The contrasting iron responses suggest another source of glial heterogeneity. Increased iron-uptake and decreased iron-export scores in iMGLs are consistent with a transcriptional tendency toward iron retention. Opposite astrocytic scores could indicate a different adaptation to amyloid pathology, although differences in species, sampling and assay design offer alternative explanations. These patterns motivate measuring iron exchange and compartmentalization in matched glial systems, rather than assuming a shared response across cell types. Ferro-aging reference expression may help organize such comparisons, but does not itself measure ferroptosis or iron-dependent injury. The primate framework (Liu et al. 2026a) supplies a related biological reference whose relevance to AD glia remains to be tested. Its correction addressed source data for Figure S2P without changing the published analyses or conclusions (Liu et al. 2026b); we retained the selected Table S2 gene-set version. These biological distinctions also shape the interpretation of YZDHD-related pharmacological candidates. Exact compound identity and experimental-record review narrowed the human intersection to five candidates and the broader program-associated set to twenty targets. Such connections provide starting points for mechanism-focused experiments, but the desired action cannot be inferred from target membership alone. For CA2, a negative disease expression association together with inhibition records raises the question of whether further inhibition would oppose or reinforce the disease-associated state. LTA4H requires attention to its dual enzyme functions, while PKM requires isoform- and site-specific assessment. For SNCA, aggregation-related observations call for assays that distinguish aggregation effects from binding to a wild-type monomer. Candidate-specific questions of this kind may be more informative than a single ranking of presumed beneficial targets. They also provide a rationale for exploring complementary actions among constituents, provided that relevant compounds and exposures can first be established.

The primary network findings temper a broad multitarget interpretation. Candidate target collections did not show significant proximity to the human association subset in the direct experimental-channel network. Incomplete target coverage and source-dependent network structure may contribute to this result, so it should not be interpreted as evidence of pharmacological inactivity. Nevertheless, the present proximity analysis offers limited support for a global human disease mechanism. Exploratory proximity to model programs may help identify experimental contexts, although shared members reduce the independence of those comparisons. Structural assessments add information about geometric compatibility, but receptor-specific issues involving metals, covalent sites, transporter conformations and aggregation models constrain their interpretation. Agreement between database links, network placement and docking would be most useful when followed by measurements of binding and functional response at relevant exposure.

Virtual knockout analyses further suggest that candidate relevance may depend on donor composition and the surrounding regulatory network. The attenuation of several initial pathway observations under resampling indicates that a response from one inferred network may not represent a reproducible biological dependency. Shared responses to reference-gene perturbations also suggest that high module disturbance can reflect network architecture or broadly responsive annotations. Improved reference matching strengthens numerical comparability, but does not by itself resolve these biological alternatives. This argues for assessing candidate-specific effects against matched perturbations and testing whether they persist across donors. In this setting, expression support, reproducibility and specificity may be more useful selection criteria than unsigned disturbance magnitude alone.

Several features strengthen the interpretability of the analysis. Donor-level aggregation preserves biological replication in the human association analysis, while cohort omission evaluates dependence on individual datasets. Keeping human disease associations separate from model-derived programs allows similarities and discrepancies to remain visible. Compound identity and assay provenance make the basis of each pharmacological connection explicit, and matched-reference perturbations challenge apparently strong candidate responses. Together, these features support a more transparent progression from a disease-associated expression pattern to a testable pharmacological hypothesis. They provide complementary checks on interpretation, rather than independent validation of every proposed mechanism.

Cell identity and replication remain important limitations. Source annotations and marker coexpression supported the retained populations, but comprehensive doublet and ambient-RNA correction was not performed. Low target expression may therefore reflect a small supported cell population, uncertain cellular origin or both. Balanced sampling cannot fully distinguish these possibilities, and bootstrap replicates or two random seeds do not add independent donors. These considerations may be particularly relevant to neurotransmitter- or synapse-related annotations in microglial profiles. They reinforce the importance of preserving biological replication in single-cell inference (Squair et al. 2021). DoubletFinder, Scrublet and SoupX offer potential approaches for addressing doublet and ambient-RNA contributions in future analyses; they were not applied here (McGinnis et al. 2019; Wolock et al. 2019; Young and Behjati 2020).

Translation to the complete preparation introduces additional uncertainty. The ingredient list lacks verified dose, preparation, batch composition and quantitative chemical measurements, so database constituents may not reflect the compounds reaching glial cells. ADMET and blood–brain barrier predictions can inform prioritization, but relevant unbound exposure remains to be measured. No formula exposure–potency comparison, direct target-engagement measurement, signed drug-induced state change or rescue experiment was available. Similarly, the absence of a qualified spatial dataset limits interpretation of directed microglia–astrocyte communication. These gaps define the conditions under which the current hypotheses could be evaluated, rather than implying a null biological effect. Experimental studies of intracellular bioavailability emphasize why physicochemical predictions alone may not describe the drug fraction available to a target (Mateus et al. 2017).

Future work could begin with chemically characterized YZDHD tested at measured exposure levels in matched microglial and astrocytic systems. Direct measurements of histone lactylation, senescence, iron pools and lipid peroxidation would help distinguish coordinated modulation from overlapping transcriptional stress responses. Target perturbation and rescue experiments could then examine whether candidate proteins mediate those changes and in which direction. Covariance-aware synthesis of paired regional effects and stronger cell-identity verification would improve the corresponding human analyses. Cellular thermal shift and live-cell kinase occupancy methods illustrate target-engagement approaches, with assay choice depending on the candidate and experimental system (Martinez Molina et al. 2013; Vasta et al. 2018). Integrating these measurements with transcriptomic responses may clarify whether YZDHD-related compounds influence complementary glial processes and help refine experimentally grounded multipathway hypotheses for AD.
